patients.summary: Administrative assistant who joins in 2021 with hypothyroidism, then develops erosive rheumatoid arthritis treated with methotrexate and prednisone, restless legs, vulvar lichen sclerosus, iron deficiency from an advanced ascending-colon adenoma, and in late 2025 a stage I diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated with R-CHOP. Sparse outside records.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
51F here to establish. Her last PCP retired over the summer and she wanted an office she could actually reach by phone.

PMH: hypothyroidism, on levothyroxine for a long time, dose stable at 100 mcg for several years per her report. No other ongoing problems.
PSH: R carpal tunnel release 2018, tonsils out as a child.
Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg qAM.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with autoimmune (Hashimoto) thyroid disease. Father had colon cancer at 65, doing ok. One sister with rheumatoid arthritis.
SH: administrative assistant, full time. Married. Quit cigarettes about 10 years ago, roughly 10 pack-years total. Doesn't drink.

ROS: energy fine, no palpitations, weight steady, bowels regular. Joints fine.

Exam: well appearing. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Skin unremarkable.

A/P
1. Hypothyroidism - stable on 100 mcg, TSH today.
2. Health maintenance - she thinks her last colonoscopy was around 2016 and was clean, done early because of her dad. Pap a couple of years ago. Mammogram last fall. Requesting old records to confirm. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time hep C and HIV screen, she agreed.
3. Former smoker, 10 pk-yr - below threshold for lung screening.
4. Mammogram ordered.

RTC 6 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jennifer, your blood work came back fine. Thyroid level is on target with the current levothyroxine, so no dose change. Blood count, kidney and liver numbers and cholesterol are all normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Glad to have you with us.

- Pap with HPV co-testing 2019: negative/negative.
- Screening mammogram 2020: BI-RADS 1.
- Tdap 05/2017.
- COVID-19 Pfizer doses 04/09/2021 and 04/30/2021 (pharmacy record).
- Levothyroxine 100 mcg with TSH values in range at each annual check.

Scanned to media, abstracted to health maintenance. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 52F.

Interval: hands. Since around April her fingers and both wrists are stiff and achy when she gets up, takes well over an hour at her desk before she can type comfortably. Gets better as she moves around, worse again after sitting through a long meeting. Some puffiness across the knuckles of the middle fingers and both wrists. No rash, no fevers, no recent illness. Sister has RA and she is worried about the same thing.

Otherwise well. Thyroid stable. Mood good.

Exam: BP and vitals as recorded. HEENT ok. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Breast exam deferred to mammogram per her preference. Hands: soft swelling over both wrists and several PIPs, tender to squeeze across the MCPs, no nodules, no deformity. Knees, ankles, feet normal.

A/P
1. Symmetric small-joint inflammatory arthritis picture with prolonged AM stiffness and a sister with RA. Referring to rheumatology for evaluation; they will want their own serologies and films so not duplicating here.
2. Hypothyroidism - TSH, continue 100 mcg.
3. Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids.
4. Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy due 2026. Pap due 2024.
5. PHQ-2 negative.
6. Flu and updated COVID shot next month at a nurse visit.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outpatient rheumatology consultation, seen 10/20/2022. Thank you for the referral.

Ms. Michaud is 52 and describes half a year of pain in the same joints on both sides, mainly the wrists and the PIPs, with swelling and morning stiffness that lasts more than an hour and loosens with use. No infection preceding it. Hypothyroid on levothyroxine. Sister with RA. NKDA. Former smoker.

On examination the involved wrists and PIPs are warm, mildly erythematous and tender, with slightly limited motion.

RF positive, anti-CCP positive. ESR 50 mm/hr. CRP 3.0 mg/dL. CBC, renal function and hepatic panel normal.

Impression: seropositive rheumatoid arthritis.

Plan: methotrexate 15 mg once weekly with folic acid 1 mg daily; prednisone 5 mg daily as a bridge. Labs every 8 to 12 weeks for methotrexate monitoring through our office. Avoid alcohol. Follow up in about two months.

Outpatient Rheumatology

documents.title: Rheumatology letter reviewed
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Rheumatology consult letter from 10/20 scanned in. Called pt to reconcile meds. She started methotrexate 6 tabs every Saturday, folic acid daily and prednisone 5 mg each morning, filled at her pharmacy. Med list updated. Reminded her no live vaccines while on methotrexate - her shingles series was the non-live one and is complete. PCP aware.

documents.title: Addendum
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Seropositive RA, on MTX/folate/low-dose pred. Give pneumococcal vaccine at her next visit given immunosuppression.

reports.text: Digital bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis compared with 10/2021. Heterogeneously dense breast tissue. No new mass, suspicious calcifications or distortion. Stable appearance.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just an update since I don't think rheum sends you their notes after the first one. Saw them on the 27th. My wrists are still sore and stiff for a good hour plus every morning, a little better than before but not much. New thing is my thumb, pointer and middle fingers go numb and tingly, mostly at night - it woke me up a couple times. When the doctor bent my wrists down and held them for a minute it brought the tingling right on. They did x-rays of both hands and said the bones are a bit thin around the joints and there are some early erosions, which I didn't love hearing. They kept me on the same methotrexate, folic acid and prednisone and want to see me in a few months. Should I be doing anything else?

documents.title: RE: Rheumatology follow up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for filling me in, that's really helpful. The finger tingling can come from swelling at the wrist pressing on the nerve, and it often settles as the arthritis gets controlled. Rheumatology is the right team to steer the RA treatment, so keep that follow-up. If the numbness becomes constant or you notice weakness or dropping things, let me know. I'll see you in March and we'll do your pneumonia vaccine then.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology outpatient consult, 05/01/2023.

53-year-old woman with RA on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone and treated hypothyroidism, referred for leg symptoms. For roughly six months she has had a deep, crawling discomfort in the legs and an urge to move them, worst in the evening and at night, eased for a time by walking or stretching. She has no back pain, weakness or numbness in the legs.

Neurological examination is normal. Peripheral pulses intact.

Labs: hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, ferritin 15 ng/mL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, TSH 2.5 mIU/L.

Assessment: restless legs syndrome. Ferritin is well below the level we aim for in RLS.

Recommendations: ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day, taken with vitamin C and away from levothyroxine by at least 4 hours. Repeat ferritin in about 3 months. Sleep hygiene discussed. Will see again as needed.

Neurology Clinic

documents.title: Referral question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is a little embarrassing. For about six months I've had really bad itching down below, on the outside, and it's worst at night. I've gone through a few tubes of the drugstore yeast cream and it hasn't touched it. No discharge, no bleeding. I'd rather see a gynecologist for this - can you put in a referral? The insurance needs one from you.

documents.title: RE: Referral question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not embarrassing at all, and it makes sense to have gynecology take a proper look since the yeast creams haven't helped. Referral placed today. If you notice any sores, bleeding or a lump before then, message me and I'll get you in here sooner.

conditions.label: Lichen sclerosus
conditions.note: clinical diagnosis by gynecology 06/22/2023; biopsy planned

documents.title: Saw the gynecologist
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw GYN yesterday. She said the skin on the vulva and around the back is thin and crinkly with white patches, and she thinks it is lichen sclerosus. No swollen glands. She wants to do a small biopsy at my next visit in August to be sure. Until then she said I can use the over the counter hydrocortisone. Just wanted you to have it for my chart.

documents.title: RE: Saw the gynecologist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you, added to your problem list as a working diagnosis. The biopsy is the right next step. Hope the itching eases a bit in the meantime.

reports.text:
Specimen: vulva, punch biopsy, submitted 08/21/2023 by outpatient gynecology. Clinical history: pruritus, white atrophic patches.

Microscopic: the epidermis is thinned with compact hyperkeratosis. The upper dermis shows a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate. No atypia.
reports.conclusion: Hyperkeratosis, atrophic epidermis and band-like dermal lymphocytic infiltrate, consistent with lichen sclerosus. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

Exam: well. Thyroid normal. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Hands with mild wrist fullness, no deformity. Skin fine. Legs no edema. GU exam deferred, gyn following.

1. RLS, low ferritin, off iron for GI side effects. Discussed retrying with a stool softener or a gentler preparation; she'd like a break for now and will bring it up with neurology. Not pushing today.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP

CC: belly cramps, bowels off.

HPI: 55F. About 2 months of crampy lower abdominal pain that lets up after she has a BM. Swings between a few days of constipation and then loose stools. Lately the cramps have been waking her at night, which is new. Not hungry - a lot of pressure at work this quarter, she's skipping lunch. Scale at home is down several pounds and it's confirmed here. events.reason: Abdominal pain, altered bowel habit, weight loss

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GI consultation, 04/14/2025.

55-year-old with hypothyroidism and RA on methotrexate and prednisone, also followed for restless legs and lichen sclerosus. Two months of lower abdominal cramping relieved by defecation, mixed constipation and diarrhea, now worse at night, and ten pounds of weight loss over the same period that she puts down to poor appetite under work stress. No travel or recent antibiotics. Father with colorectal cancer at 65. Last colonoscopy 2016, normal.

Exam: abdomen soft, mild diffuse tenderness, no rebound or guarding. Rectal exam unremarkable.

Labs: hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 15 ng/mL, CRP 8 mg/L, tissue transglutaminase IgA negative.

Assessment: microcytic iron deficiency anemia with altered bowel habit and weight loss; celiac serology negative. A colonic source needs to be excluded.

Plan: colonoscopy, scheduled 05/08. Ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. We will send the report.

Outpatient Gastroenterology

conditions.label: Benign neoplasm of ascending colon
conditions.note: 22 mm tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia, resected by EMR

reports.text:
Specimen: ascending colon polyp, endoscopic mucosal resection, piecemeal, multiple fragments up to 1.4 cm in aggregate 2.3 cm.

Microscopic: adenomatous epithelium with tubular and villous architecture. Foci of high-grade dysplasia. No invasive carcinoma identified in the material examined.
reports.conclusion: Tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia. Negative for invasive carcinoma.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Colonoscopy 05/08/2025. Indication: iron deficiency anemia, change in bowel habit, weight loss, family history of colorectal cancer.

Monitored anesthesia care. Prep good. Cecum reached and identified by appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve; terminal ileum not intubated. Withdrawal time 14 minutes.

Findings: a 22 mm sessile polyp in the ascending colon, lifted with submucosal injection and removed by endoscopic mucosal resection in several pieces; defect margins inspected with no visible residual tissue; defect closed with 3 clips. The remainder of the colon was normal to the cecum. Retroflexion in the rectum unremarkable.

Impression: large ascending colon polyp, resected. No other abnormality.

Recommendations: await pathology. Continue iron. Because the resection was piecemeal, repeat colonoscopy in about 6 months to check the site. Copy to PCP.

conditions.label: History of adenomatous colon polyps
conditions.note: advanced adenoma (tubulovillous, high-grade dysplasia), ascending colon

documents.title: Colonoscopy and pathology reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: GI report and pathology arrived today. 22 mm ascending colon polyp removed piecemeal, tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia, no cancer. Called her - relieved. This is the likely bleeding source for her iron deficiency. Reviewed: keep taking iron daily, GI wants a look at the site in ~6 months. Suggested she let her sister know, since with their dad's history this is worth mentioning to her own doctor. Recheck CBC and ferritin in July.

orders.reason: left cervical lymphadenopathy with B symptoms

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED visit 10/21/2025, brief summary.

55F with hypothyroidism, RA on methotrexate and prednisone, and a colon adenoma removed earlier this year. Two months of night sweats, low-grade fevers at home and about 10 lb of weight loss she was not trying for. Has felt a lump on the left side of her neck that has slowly grown. Home meds as listed by patient: levothyroxine, folic acid. NKDA.

Exam: firm, rubbery, non-tender 3 cm lymph node in the left cervical chain. No hepatosplenomegaly.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, WBC 7,000, platelets 250,000, LDH 245, ESR 50, ANA positive, RF elevated.

Impression: cervical lymphadenopathy with constitutional symptoms, concerning for lymphoma.

Disposition: stable for discharge. Urgent outpatient excisional node biopsy arranged with general surgery. Return for high fevers, trouble swallowing or breathing. PCP notified.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read the ED note and called her. Frightened but organized. Surgery has her for excisional biopsy of the left neck node on 10/30. Explained what the biopsy tells us and that I'll call as soon as pathology is back. She asked about her methotrexate - told her not to change anything until we have a diagnosis and rheum weighs in. Reminded her she can call or text me directly with questions.

events.reason: Excisional biopsy, left cervical lymph node

conditions.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, lymph nodes of head, face, and neck

reports.text:
Specimen: lymph node, left neck, excisional biopsy. Received fresh, 3.2 x 2.4 x 1.9 cm.

Microscopic: nodal architecture is effaced by a diffuse proliferation of large lymphoid cells. Immunohistochemistry supports a B-cell lineage.

documents.title: Surgical pathology received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Lymph node pathology from general surgery (biopsy 10/30) received by fax. Flagged urgent to PCP.

documents.title: Lymph node pathology discussed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with her husband on speaker. Node shows diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Talked through what that means in plain terms: an aggressive but often curable lymphoma, treatment is usually chemo-immunotherapy, staging scan comes first. Urgent heme/onc referral placed, they can see her Monday 11/10. Called rheumatology to let them know given methotrexate; they will coordinate with oncology on stopping it. She knows to reach me any time.

medications.reason: stopped at lymphoma diagnosis with rheumatology agreement

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Hematology/Oncology new patient consultation, 11/10/2025.

Diagnosis: diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, left cervical lymph node, excised 10/30/2025.

55-year-old woman with seropositive RA treated with methotrexate and prednisone, hypothyroidism, and an advanced colon adenoma removed in May. Two months of night sweats, low-grade fevers and 10 lb weight loss with an enlarging left neck node.

Staging: PET-CT 11/07/2025 shows FDG-avid lymph nodes in the left neck only, the largest 3.1 cm. No other nodal or extranodal disease; bone marrow and spleen not involved. Stage I with B symptoms.

Pre-treatment: hepatitis B surface antigen and core antibody negative. HIV negative. Echocardiogram LVEF 60%.

Plan: methotrexate stopped today in agreement with her rheumatologist; folic acid stopped with it. R-CHOP every 21 days for 6 cycles, first cycle 11/13/2025. She continues prednisone 5 mg daily on the days she is not taking the chemotherapy prednisone. Restaging PET after completion. Supportive medicines will be prescribed by our clinic.

Thank you for referring her.
Hematology/Oncology

documents.title: Two down
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just checking in - second round of chemo was last Thursday. Tired for about a week after each one and some nausea the first few days, the oncology nurses gave me medicine for it and it mostly works. The lump in my neck already feels smaller. Joints feel better than they have in ages, oddly. I'm working from home on the bad days.

documents.title: RE: Two down
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: So good to hear the node is shrinking already. Lean on the oncology team for nausea or fevers - a fever during chemo is a call-them-right-away situation. Let's do a short video check-in in January.

Hypothyroidism - stable, TSH at next in-person visit.
RA quiet off methotrexate.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Hematology/Oncology follow-up.

DLBCL, stage I with B symptoms, left neck. Completed R-CHOP x6 on 02/26/2026.

End-of-treatment PET-CT 04/09/2026: complete metabolic response, Deauville 2. No residual FDG-avid disease.

She feels well, energy returning, no night sweats or fevers.

Plan: surveillance visits with exam and labs every 3 months for the first two years. Routine imaging not planned unless symptoms. Rheumatology to manage RA from here.
Hematology/Oncology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First in-person visit since finishing chemo. PET in April showed complete response. Energy maybe 80%. Back at the office full time. No sweats, fevers or new lumps. Saw rheumatology 4/28: joints quiet since the chemo, staying on prednisone 5 mg alone, no new arthritis drug for now, they'll revisit if she flares. Bowels normal. Surveillance colonoscopy got pushed by chemo, now set for June.

Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg, prednisone 5 mg, ferrous sulfate 325 mg, clobetasol twice weekly.

O: weight 64 kg. Neck without adenopathy. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Hands without synovitis.

A/P
1. DLBCL in complete metabolic response - oncology surveillance q3mo.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - CBC, ferritin.
3. Hypothyroidism - TSH.
4. RA - on prednisone alone per rheum.
5. Adenoma surveillance - colonoscopy June.
Annual in September.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 12.4, ferritin 58 - anemia resolved and stores recovering. TSH normal. Kidney and liver tests normal. Continue iron for now, messaged her.

reports.text:
Specimen: ascending colon, resection scar, cold forceps biopsies, three fragments.

Microscopic: colonic mucosa with preserved crypt architecture and mild submucosal fibrosis. No adenomatous change.
reports.conclusion: Benign colonic mucosa. Negative for adenoma and dysplasia.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Surveillance colonoscopy 06/11/2026, one year after piecemeal EMR of a 22 mm tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia (interval extended for lymphoma treatment).

Prep adequate. Cecum reached. Clipped resection scar in the ascending colon, flat and pale, with no residual polyp; scar biopsied. Remainder of the colon normal.

Impression: no residual adenoma at the EMR site.
Recommendation: repeat colonoscopy in 1 year. Copy to PCP.
